title: Ballade des pendus (Épitaphe Villon)
author: François Villon
source_notes: Middle French original; Swinburne's 1878 verse translation. Both public domain.
reading_notes: Composed in prison, perhaps before an expected execution, Villon speaks in the voice of the dead on the gibbet, asking the living for pity. Notice the Middle French spelling (piéça, mercis) and the insistent refrain ending each stanza: a plea that God absolve all.

lines.original: Frères humains qui après nous vivez,
lines.english: Men, brother men, that after us yet live,
lines.gloss: Frères = 'brothers'; humains = 'human' (plural adjective); qui = 'who' (relative); après nous = 'after us'; vivez = 'live' (2nd plural of vivre).

lines.original: N'ayez les cœurs contre nous endurcis,
lines.english: Let not your hearts too hard against us be;
lines.gloss: N'ayez = 'do not have' (negative imperative of avoir); les cœurs = 'the hearts'; contre nous = 'against us'; endurcis = 'hardened' (past participle).

lines.original: Car, si pitié de nous pauvres avez,
lines.english: For if some pity of us poor men ye give,
lines.gloss: Car = 'for'; si = 'if'; pitié = 'pity' (noun); de nous pauvres = 'of us poor ones'; avez = 'have' (2nd plural of avoir).

lines.original: Dieu en aura plus tôt de vous mercis.
lines.english: The sooner God shall take of you pity.
lines.gloss: Dieu = 'God'; en = 'of it' (pronoun); aura = 'will have' (future of avoir); plus tôt = 'sooner'; de vous = 'of you'; mercis = 'mercy, mercies' (Middle French plural of merci).

lines.original: Vous nous voyez ci attachés cinq, six :
lines.english: Here are we five or six strung up, you see,
lines.gloss: Vous = 'you'; nous = 'us'; voyez = 'see' (voir); ci = 'here' (archaic); attachés = 'attached, hung'; cinq, six = 'five, six'.

lines.original: Quant de la chair, que trop avons nourrie,
lines.english: And flesh that we too well had cherished, lo!
lines.gloss: Quant de = 'as for'; la chair = 'the flesh'; que = 'which'; trop = 'too much'; avons nourrie = 'we have nourished' (feminine past participle agreement).

lines.original: Elle est piéça dévorée et pourrie,
lines.english: It is long eaten out and rotten through.
lines.gloss: Elle = 'it' (refers to chair); est = 'is'; piéça = 'long ago' (archaic); dévorée = 'devoured' (feminine past participle); pourrie = 'rotted'.

lines.original: Et nous, les os, devenons cendre et poudre.
lines.english: And we the bones grow dust and ash anew.
lines.gloss: nous = 'we'; les os = 'the bones'; devenons = 'become' (devenir); cendre = 'ash'; poudre = 'dust, powder'.

lines.original: De notre mal personne ne s'en rie ;
lines.english: Let no man laugh at us discomforted,
lines.gloss: De notre mal = 'at our misfortune'; personne = 'nobody'; ne ... s'en rie = 'let him not laugh at it' (subjunctive of se rire).

lines.original: Mais priez Dieu que tous nous veuille absoudre !
lines.english: But pray to God that he forgive us all.
lines.gloss: Mais = 'but'; priez = 'pray!' (imperative of prier); Dieu = 'God'; que = 'that'; tous nous = 'us all'; veuille = 'may be willing' (subjunctive of vouloir); absoudre = 'to absolve'.

lines.original: Se frères vous clamons, pas n'en devez
lines.english: If we call you brothers, ye should not take
lines.gloss: Se = 'if' (Middle French si); frères = 'brothers'; vous = 'you'; clamons = 'call, name' (1st plural); pas n'en devez = 'you must not from it' (archaic negation).

lines.original: Avoir dédain, quoique fûmes occis
lines.english: Offence, even though slain by law's hand
lines.gloss: Avoir dédain = 'to have scorn' (infinitive); quoique = 'although'; fûmes occis = 'we were killed' (past simple passive of occire, archaic).

lines.original: Par justice. Toutefois, vous savez
lines.english: Were we. You know right well, I trow,
lines.gloss: Par justice = 'by justice'; Toutefois = 'however'; vous savez = 'you know' (savoir).

lines.original: Que tous hommes n'ont pas bon sens rassis ;
lines.english: That not all men have wit at their command;
lines.gloss: Que = 'that'; tous hommes = 'all men'; n'ont pas = 'have not'; bon sens = 'good sense'; rassis = 'settled, steady'.

lines.original: Excusez-nous, puisque sommes transis,
lines.english: Excuse us then, who now are hence departed,
lines.gloss: Excusez-nous = 'excuse us!' (imperative); puisque = 'since'; sommes transis = 'we are stunned, chilled, numb' (archaic).

lines.original: Envers le fils de la Vierge Marie,
lines.english: To the Son of the Virgin Mary turn,
lines.gloss: Envers = 'toward'; le fils de la Vierge Marie = 'the son of the Virgin Mary' (accusative sense).

lines.original: Que sa grâce ne soit pour nous tarie,
lines.english: That his grace for us be not exhausted,
lines.gloss: Que = 'that'; sa grâce = 'his grace'; ne soit tarie = 'not be dried up' (subjunctive of être + tarir).

lines.original: Nous préservant de l'infernale foudre.
lines.english: Preserving us from the infernal fire.
lines.gloss: Nous préservant = 'preserving us' (present participle); de l'infernale foudre = 'from the infernal bolt/fire'.

lines.original: Nous sommes morts, âme ne nous harie,
lines.english: We are dead; let no soul persecute us,
lines.gloss: sommes morts = 'are dead' (past participle of mourir); âme = 'soul' (nominative subject); ne nous harie = 'let not harass us' (subjunctive of harier, archaic).

lines.original: Mais priez Dieu que tous nous veuille absoudre !
lines.english: But pray to God that he forgive us all.
lines.gloss: Repeat of the refrain; see line 10 for word-by-word gloss.
